hypothesis: IPA phonetic notation (47 symbols) could enable smaller vocabularies than standard tokenization (1024 tokens), allowing larger models within 16MB budget

disambiguation_test.key_observation: Model learned contextual patterns despite identical IPA for homophones

conversion_costs.conclusion: Currently costs more space than it saves

key_findings: IPA is trainable - loss dropped 89% in 500 steps
Homophones remain a fundamental limitation (knight/night identical)
Context-based disambiguation shows promise (40% accuracy on tiny model)
eng_to_ipa library (~3MB) negates the embedding savings
challenges: Homophones: knight/night/to/too/two become identical in IPA
Unknown words: ~5.7% of tokens marked with *
Conversion library size: 3MB is too large for 16MB budget
Proper nouns: Poor handling of names and technical terms
Evaluation: Need IPA↔English conversion for validation
recommendations: Build minimal IPA converter (<500KB) to make space tradeoff positive
Consider hybrid: 1024 vocab + IPA tokens for phonetic patterns
Test on validation set to measure actual bits-per-byte impact
Investigate whether context is sufficient for good predictions
verdict: Partially viable but requires significant optimization of conversion tables to be competitive
